beginner.summary: For developers who already program in a language such as Python, Java, C#, Go or C and are new to Rust. Covers the rustup and Cargo toolchain on Rust 1.100 with the 2024 edition, ownership, borrowing and slices, scalar and text types, structs, enums and pattern matching, error handling with Result and Option, collections, traits and generics, lifetimes in simple functions, closures and iterators, Box and Rc, modules, crates and Cargo.toml, testing, and a command-line tool capstone.
prerequisites: Writes working programs in at least one other language such as Python, Java, C#, Go or C
Uses a terminal confidently: changing directories, running commands and setting environment variables
Has a Windows, macOS or Linux laptop with rights to install rustup, a C linker (Visual Studio Build Tools on Windows, Xcode Command Line Tools on macOS) and an editor such as Visual Studio Code
outcomes: Install and manage a Rust toolchain with rustup and build, run, test and document packages with Cargo
Write programs that pass the borrow checker by applying ownership, borrowing, slices and simple lifetime annotations
Model data with structs, enums, traits and generics, and handle failure with Result, Option and the ? operator
Build and test a command-line tool that reads files, uses crates from crates.io and reports errors with correct exit codes
